stem: Zubin lines up $25$ closed school lockers numbered $1$ to $25$. Student $k$ toggles every $k$-th locker, for $k=1,2,\ldots,25$, starting from all closed.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names the lockers that remain open?

options.text: Only the prime-numbered lockers remain open.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A locker ends open exactly when it is toggled an odd number of times, which happens only for square numbers; the squares from 1 to 25 are 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25.

teacher.key_rationale: Toggle count equals the number of factors. Only perfect squares have an odd number of factors, so lockers 1,4,9,16,25 stay open.
